newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico bourse sharply down on Brazil fallout.
newsitem.headline: Mexico bourse sharply down on Brazil fallout.

text.p: Mexican stocks sharply extended their initial slump in early trade on Tuesday due to widespread concerns that sharp falls on the Brazilian stock markets could lead to a lack of confidence in Latin American markets in general, analysts and dealers said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was down 88.29 points, or 1.85 percent, at 4,688.78.
The Sao Paulo stock market had meanwhile fallen 873 points to 11,825.
For Jorge Mariscal, Chief of Investment Strategy for Latin America at Goldman Sachs, the reaction in Mexico was more automatic than fundamental.
"There has been no fundamental change in risk perception for Mexico," he said. "The Brazil effect is spreading."
Marsical noted that trading volume .TV.MX was thin at 13.2 million shares and did not mean investors were bailing out of Mexico.
Mariscal was meanwhile cautiously optimistic sharp falls in share prices could represent a buying opportunity.

Dealers said they feared a "tequila effect" in reverse, referring to the Mexican peso devaluation crisis of December 1994 which spawned a sharp increase in risk perception for Latin American markets in general.
Dealers said market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), down 45 centavos to 20.35, was leading the slide. Telmex accounted for about one-quarter of all shares traded in early dealing.
